# Importing Data

```{r}
# Importing data sets
FRED3 <- read.csv("FRED3.csv")
FRED4 <- read.csv("FRED4_Entire_Database_2026.csv")
FRED_newest <- readr::read_csv("FRED_NEWEST.csv", 
                        locale = readr::locale(encoding = "latin1"))

AU <- read.csv("AUwarming.csv")
```

# Cleaning Data

## FRED 3.0 Cleaning

```{r, warning = FALSE}
# FRED 3 data cleaning

# make first row the header
FRED3 <- FRED3 |> row_to_names(1)

# remove irrelevant rows
FRED3 <- FRED3 |>
  filter(Name == "1" | Name == "Type")

# pulling the first row as a vector 
var_type <- unlist(FRED3[1,], use.names = FALSE)

# get vector of indices that correspond to root traits
indices <- rep(0, length(var_type))

# looping through entire row of variable types
for (i in 1:length(var_type)) {
  
  # if entry is empty
  if(is.na(var_type[i])){
    # skip that entry
    i = i + 1
  }
  # if the variable type is root trait
  else if (var_type[i] == "Root_Traits") {
   
    # add the index to our vector
    indices[i] <- i

  }
}

# dropping "0" values from indices vector
indices <- indices[indices != 0]

# dplyr::selecting columns with article, lat, long, and root traits
FRED3_cleaned <- FRED3 |>
  # create short variable name for article
  rename(Article = "Abbreviated article citation", 
         order = "Plant taxonomy_Accepted order_APW",
         family = "Plant taxonomy_Accepted family_TPL", 
         genus = "Plant taxonomy_Accepted genus_TPL", 
         species = "Plant Taxonomy_Accepted species_TPL") |>
  # select article, coordinates, and root trait columns
  dplyr::select(Article, Latitude_Main, Longitude_Main,
                order, family, genus, species, indices) 
 
# removing the row that was "type"
FRED3_cleaned <- FRED3_cleaned[3:nrow(FRED3_cleaned),]

# keeping only non-empty columns
FRED3_cleaned <- FRED3_cleaned |>
  select(where(~ any(!is.na(.) & . != "")))

```

## FRED 4.0 Cleaning


```{r, warning = FALSE}
# FRED 4 data cleaning

# making first row replace the header
FRED4 <- FRED4 |> row_to_names(1)

# remove irrelevant rows
FRED4 <- FRED4 |>
  filter(`Version_FRED version number` == "4" | 
           `Version_FRED version number` == "2" |
           `Version_FRED version number` == "3" |
           `Version_FRED version number` == "1" |
           `Notes_Row ID` == "Meta_Data")

# pulling the first row as a vector 
var_type <- unlist(FRED4[1,], use.names = FALSE)

# get vector of indices that correspond to root traits
indices <- rep(0, length(var_type))

# looping through entire row of variable types
for (i in 1:length(var_type)) {
  
  # if entry is empty
  if(is.na(var_type[i])){
    # skip that entry
    i = i + 1
  } 
  # if the variable type is root trait
  else if (var_type[i] == "Root_Traits") {
   
    # add the index to our vector
    indices[i] <- i

  }
}

# dropping "0" values from indices vector
indices <- indices[indices != 0]

# selecting columns with article, lat, long, and root traits
FRED4_cleaned <- FRED4 |>
   # create short variable name for article
  rename(Article = "Abbreviated article citation",
         citation = "Data source_Citation",
         order = "Plant taxonomy_Accepted order_WFO",
         family = "Plant taxonomy_Accepted family_WFO", 
         genus = "Plant taxonomy_Accepted genus_WFO", 
         species = "Plant Taxonomy_Accepted species_WFO",
         growth = "Plant growth form_TRY") |>
  # select article, coordinates, and root trait columns
  dplyr::select(Article, citation, Latitude_Main, Longitude_Main,
                order, family, genus, species, growth,
                indices)

# removing the row that represented "type"
FRED4_cleaned <- FRED4_cleaned[3:nrow(FRED4_cleaned),]

# keeping only non-empty columns
FRED4_cleaned <- FRED4_cleaned |>
  select(where(~ any(!is.na(.) & . != "")))

```

## Stats about the FRED 3, 4.0 and 4.1

### FRED 3.0 Arctic Stats

```{r}
FRED3_arctic <- FRED3_cleaned |>
  mutate(Latitude_Main = as.numeric(Latitude_Main),
         Longitude_Main = as.numeric(Longitude_Main)) |>
  filter(
    # Global baseline: Everything north of 66.5333
    (Latitude_Main >= 66.5333 & Latitude_Main <= 90.0) |
    
    # North America exception: North of 60°N between 20W and 170W
    (Latitude_Main >= 60.0 & Latitude_Main < 66.5333 & 
       Longitude_Main >= -170 & Longitude_Main <= -20) |
    
    # Asia exception: North of 62N between 60E and 180E 
    (Latitude_Main >= 62.0 & Latitude_Main < 66.5333 & 
       ((Longitude_Main >= 60 & Longitude_Main <= 180) | 
        (Longitude_Main >= -180 & Longitude_Main <= -170)))
  )

FRED3_arctic |>
  distinct(Article) |>
  nrow()

FRED3_unique_species <- FRED3_arctic |>
  select(genus, species) |>
  distinct(genus, species, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ na_if(str_trim(.x), ""))) |>
  distinct(genus, species, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  remove_empty(which = "rows") |>
  nrow()

FRED3_unique_species

FRED3_unique_coord <- FRED3_arctic |>
  select(Latitude_Main, Longitude_Main) |>
  drop_na(Latitude_Main, Longitude_Main) |>
  filter(
    Latitude_Main != "unspecified",
    Longitude_Main != "unspecified"
  ) |>
  distinct() |>
  nrow()

FRED3_unique_coord

FRED3arctic_sf <- st_as_sf(
  FRED3_arctic,
  coords = c("Longitude_Main", "Latitude_Main"),
  crs = 4326,
  remove = FALSE # Keeps  original coordinate columns in the output
)

# get the world map data
countries_sf <- ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf")

# spatial join to find which country polygon each point sits inside
# adds 'country_name' and 'country_iso' to  data
FRED3arctic_with_countries <- st_join(
  FRED3arctic_sf,
  countries_sf[, c("name", "iso_a3")]
)

# Rename the new columns for clarity
names(FRED3arctic_with_countries)[names(FRED3arctic_with_countries) == "name"] <- "Country_Name"
names(FRED3arctic_with_countries)[names(FRED3arctic_with_countries) == "iso_a3"] <- "Country_ISO"

# convert back to a regular data frame/tibble
FRED3arctic_with_countries <- as.data.frame(FRED3arctic_with_countries)

range(FRED3arctic_with_countries$Latitude_Main, na.rm = TRUE)
range(FRED3arctic_with_countries$Longitude_Main, na.rm = TRUE)

FRED3arctic_country <- FRED3arctic_with_countries |>
  select(Latitude_Main, Longitude_Main, Country_Name) |>
  drop_na(Country_Name) |>
  distinct(Country_Name)

FRED3arctic_country$Country_Name

FRED3arctic_countryyr <- FRED3arctic_with_countries |>
  mutate(year = str_extract(Article, "[0-9]{4}"))

range(FRED3arctic_countryyr$year, na.rm = TRUE)

FRED3distinctyr <- FRED3arctic_countryyr |>
  distinct(year)

count(FRED3distinctyr)

```

### FRED 4.0 Stats

```{r}

FRED4_arctic <- FRED4_cleaned |>
  mutate(Latitude_Main = as.numeric(Latitude_Main),
         Longitude_Main = as.numeric(Longitude_Main)) |>
  filter(
    # Global baseline: Everything north of 66.5333
    (Latitude_Main >= 66.5333 & Latitude_Main <= 90.0) |
    
    # North America exception: North of 60N between 20W and 170W
    (Latitude_Main >= 60.0 & Latitude_Main < 66.5333 & 
       Longitude_Main >= -170 & Longitude_Main <= -20) |
    
    # Asia exception: North of 62N between 60E and 180E 
    (Latitude_Main >= 62.0 & Latitude_Main < 66.5333 & 
       ((Longitude_Main >= 60 & Longitude_Main <= 180) | 
        (Longitude_Main >= -180 & Longitude_Main <= -170)))
  )

FRED4_arctic |>
  distinct(Article) |>
  nrow()

FRED4_unique_species <- FRED4_arctic |>
  select(genus, species) |>
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ na_if(str_trim(.x), ""))) |>
  distinct(genus, species, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  remove_empty(which = "rows") |>
  nrow()

# FRED4_unique_species <- FRED4_arctic |>
#   select(species) |>
#   mutate(across(everything(), ~ na_if(str_trim(.x), ""))) |>
#   distinct(species, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
#   remove_empty(which = "rows") |>
#   nrow()

# Unique sampling coordinates
FRED4_unique_coord <- FRED4_arctic |>
  select(Latitude_Main, Longitude_Main) |>
  drop_na(Latitude_Main, Longitude_Main) |>
  distinct() |>
  nrow()

FRED4arctic_sf <- st_as_sf(
  FRED4_arctic,
  coords = c("Longitude_Main", "Latitude_Main"),
  crs = 4326,
  remove = FALSE # Keeps  original coordinate columns in the output
)

# get the world map data
countries_sf <- ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf")

# spatial join to find which country polygon each point sits inside
# adds 'country_name' and 'country_iso' to  data
FRED4arctic_with_countries <- st_join(
  FRED4arctic_sf,
  countries_sf[, c("name", "iso_a3")]
)

# Rename the new columns for clarity
names(FRED4arctic_with_countries)[names(FRED4arctic_with_countries) == "name"] <- "Country_Name"
names(FRED4arctic_with_countries)[names(FRED4arctic_with_countries) == "iso_a3"] <- "Country_ISO"

# convert back to a regular data frame/tibble
FRED4arctic_with_countries <- as.data.frame(FRED4arctic_with_countries)

# Countries represented
FRED4_num_countries <- FRED4arctic_with_countries |>
  drop_na(Country_Name) |>
  distinct(Country_Name) |>
  nrow()

FRED4arctic_countryyr <- FRED4arctic_with_countries |>
  mutate(
    Article = str_replace(Article,
                          "Shaver & Billlings 197$",
                          "Shaver & Billlings 1975"),
    year = str_extract(Article, "[0-9]{4}")
  )

# Years represented
FRED4_num_years <- FRED4arctic_countryyr |>
  drop_na(year) |>
  distinct(year) |>
  nrow()

# Number of articles
FRED4_num_articles <- FRED4_arctic |>
  distinct(Article) |>
  nrow()
table1 <- tibble(
  Statistic = c(
    "Articles",
    "Unique genus and species",
    "Unique coordinates",
    "Countries represented",
    "Years represented"
  ),
  Value = c(
    FRED4_num_articles,
    FRED4_unique_species,
    FRED4_unique_coord,
    FRED4_num_countries,
    FRED4_num_years
  )
)

table1 |>
  kbl(
    align = c("l", "c"),
    booktabs = TRUE
  ) |>
  kable_styling(
    full_width = FALSE,
    position = "center",
    font_size = 11
  )
```

# Graphs

## Full FRED Map

```{r}

fullfred_map <- FRED4arctic_with_countries |>
  distinct(Article, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  filter(
    !is.na(Latitude_Main),
    !is.na(Longitude_Main)
  ) 

sites_sf <- st_as_sf(
  fullfred_map,
  coords = c("Longitude_Main", "Latitude_Main"),
  crs = 4326,
  remove = FALSE
)

world <- ne_countries(
  scale = "medium",
  returnclass = "sf"
)

sites_country <- st_join(
  sites_sf,
  world[, "name"]
)

country_counts <- sites_country |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  distinct(Article, name) |>
  count(name, name = "n_articles")

world_counts <- world |>
  left_join(country_counts, by = "name")

world_counts$n_articles[is.na(world_counts$n_articles)] <- 0

arctic_crs <- 3995

world_arctic <- st_transform(world_counts, arctic_crs)
sites_arctic <- st_transform(sites_country, arctic_crs)

ggplot() +
  # Base Map Layer 
  geom_sf(
    data = world_arctic,
    aes(fill = n_articles),
    color = "grey40",
    linewidth = 0.1
  ) +
  scale_fill_distiller(
    palette = "Purples",
    direction = 1,
    name = "Articles"
  ) +
  
  # Clear fill scale for next layer
  new_scale_fill() +
  
  # Points Layer
  geom_sf(
    data = sites_arctic,
    shape = 21,             
    fill = "red",       
    colour = "black",     
    size = 1.5,             
    stroke = 0.6                           
  ) +
  coord_sf(
    xlim = c(-4e6, 4e6),
    ylim = c(-4e6, 4e6)
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```


```{r}
# Points colored by growth form

fullfred_map <- FRED4arctic_with_countries |>
  filter(
    !is.na(Latitude_Main),
    !is.na(Longitude_Main)
  ) |>
  # Clean so that same growth form collapses together
  mutate(
    # Clean up whitespace and force lowercase
    growth_clean = str_to_lower(str_trim(growth)),
    growth_clean = case_when(
      is.na(growth_clean) ~ "unspecified",
      growth_clean == "" ~ "unspecified",
      growth_clean == "unspecified" ~ "unspecified",
      # if entry is entirely blank or just spaces, call it unspecified
      str_detect(growth_clean, "^\\s*$") ~ "unspecified", 
      str_detect(growth_clean, "fern") ~ "shrub", 
      str_detect(growth_clean, "herb/shrub") ~ "shrub", 
      str_detect(growth_clean, "shrub/tree") ~ "tree", 
      TRUE ~ growth_clean
    )
  ) |>  # Distinct by BOTH Article and the cleaned growth form
  distinct(Article, growth_clean, .keep_all = TRUE)

sites_sf <- st_as_sf(
  fullfred_map,
  coords = c("Longitude_Main", "Latitude_Main"),
  crs = 4326,
  remove = FALSE
)

sites_country <- st_join(
  sites_sf,
  world[, "name"]
)

# distinct Articles are counted for the background fill
country_counts <- sites_country |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  distinct(Article, name) |> 
  count(name, name = "n_articles")

world_counts <- world |> left_join(country_counts, by = "name")
world_counts$n_articles[is.na(world_counts$n_articles)] <- 0

world_arctic <- st_transform(world_counts, arctic_crs)
sites_arctic <- st_transform(sites_country, arctic_crs)

ggplot() +
  # Base Map Layer
  geom_sf(
    data = world_arctic,
    aes(fill = n_articles),
    color = "grey40",
    linewidth = 0.1
  ) +
  scale_fill_distiller(
    palette = "Purples",
    direction = 1,
    name = "Articles"
  ) +
  
  # Clear fill scale for next layer
  new_scale_fill() +
  
  # Points color-coded by growth form
  geom_sf(
    data = sites_arctic,
      aes(fill = growth_clean),
      shape = 21,
      size = 2.5,
      stroke = 0.5,
      colour = "black"
                         
  ) + 
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = c(
      "graminoid" = "#FFD700",   # Bright Gold / Yellow (cuts through dark purple)
      "herb"      = "#E8FFF3",   # Spring Green (pops against mid/dark tones)
      "shrub"     = "#FF6B6B",   # Coral Red/Pink (high contrast on light purple)
      "tree"      = "#00E5FF",    # Electric Cyan/Aqua (extreme contrast on dark purple)
      "unspecified"  = "#B2BABB"
    ),
    name = "Growth Form")+         # Pure crisp white for NA values to completely stand out
  # scale_fill_brewer(
  #   palette = "Set2",
  #   name = "Growth Form",
  #   na.value = "grey70"       # "unspecified" or NA entries will show as a neutral grey
  # ) +
  coord_sf(
    xlim = c(-4e6, 4e6),
    ylim = c(-4e6, 4e6)
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```


## Articles Per Year

```{r}

# aggregate data by Year and Category
yearly_trends <- FRED4arctic_with_countries |>
  # Ensure we only count each article once 
  distinct(Article, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  # Clean up and extract the 4-digit year from the citation
  mutate(Article = str_replace(Article,
                          "Shaver & Billlings 197$",
                          "Shaver & Billlings 1975"),
    Year = as.numeric(str_extract(Article, "[0-9]{4}"))
  ) |>
  group_by(Year) |>
  summarise(Paper_Count = n(), .groups = "drop")

# plot the timeline trend
ggplot(yearly_trends, aes(x = Year, y = Paper_Count)) +
  # Move fill directly inside geom_col to apply it uniformly to all bars
  geom_col(width = 1, fill = "#00A5CF", color = "black", linewidth = 0.2) + 
  
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1920, 2025, by = 10)) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    # Skips by 2
    breaks = seq(0, max(yearly_trends$Paper_Count, na.rm = TRUE) + 2, by = 2)
  ) + 
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    x = "Publication Year",
    y = "Number of Papers" 
  ) +
  theme(
    text = element_text(size = 11)
  )

decade_trends <- yearly_trends |>
  mutate(Decade = floor(Year / 10) * 10) |>
  group_by(Decade) |>
  summarise(Paper_Count = sum(Paper_Count), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(decade_trends, aes(x = factor(Decade), y = Paper_Count)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#00A5CF", color = "black", linewidth = 0.2) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    x = "Decade",
    y = "Number of Papers"
  ) +
  theme(
    text = element_text(size = 11)
  )


```

## Root traits measured

```{r}
fullfred_arctic_pivot <- FRED4arctic_with_countries |> 
  # select non-empty columns
  dplyr::select(-Latitude_Main, -Longitude_Main,-geometry,
                -order, -family, -genus, -species, -growth,
                -Elevation) |>
  # keep columns article, lat, long and only pivot root trait columns (#4-738)
  pivot_longer(cols = 2:680,
               names_to = "Trait",
               values_to = "Value",
               values_drop_na = TRUE) |>
  # turn all empty cells into NAs
  mutate_all(na_if, "") |>
  # remove NAs
  drop_na()

countsbyrt <- fullfred_arctic_pivot |>
  # keep only numeric values
  mutate(Value = as.numeric(Value)) |>
  drop_na(Value) |>
  group_by(Article) |>
  summarize(Type = unique(Trait), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(Type) |>
  summarize(Count = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  slice_max(Count, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  mutate(Type = str_replace_all(Type, "_", " "))

ggplot(
  countsbyrt,
  aes(x = Count, y = reorder(Type, Count))
) +
  geom_col(fill = "darkgreen") + 
  labs(
    x = "Number of Articles that Record the Root Trait",
    y = "Root Trait Name"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```
